content.thinking: I need to correct the citation to reference AL1 instead of A1, drop the "24 hours" mention, and avoid stating specific numbers like "three replicas." I'll use AL1 as the label and T8/T9 to indicate no changes.

action_items.item: Fix the division by zero in the spend summary code (spend_summary.py) by guarding the zero divisor, and add a test that covers that input before the flag is enabled again.
Roll out flags like monthly-spend-feature to a small share of traffic first, with an automatic rollback if the error rate on the affected pages rises.
Include feature-flag toggles from the flag provider in the production change events the Investigator queries, so a flag change near the onset shows up as a change.

Make the post-action check wait for its stated window before judging a mitigation. Do not let the incident be closed while that verification is pending, and re-check the error rate after the flag revert to confirm recovery.
Add an alert or dashboard annotation that links a flag toggle to a jump in error rate on the same service, so it surfaces before the paging rule's wait ends.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers saw account page requests fail. The error rate went from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} on average while broken, peaking at {errors_at_worst}. That is {errors_rise} of traffic failing that otherwise would not have, and the service still looked at the incident's level when Argus last checked.
The failing requests each raised ZeroDivisionError (division by zero) in the spend summary code, spend_summary.py. These errors appear from the onset at {began} through the end of the window read.

That code path ran because the monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on. Before the onset the service logged the flag as off. From the onset it logged evaluations as on. The change feed shows the flag switched on by admin.

Other explanations were ruled out. The change-event query for the day before the onset returned no deploy or release on the service. The ClientDisconnected errors were shoppers closing connections, and they were logged before the onset. All replicas ran on the same GPU type, so nothing pointed at placement. The record does not show why the spend summary code divides by zero, for example which accounts or inputs give a zero divisor. The chain stops here.

contributing_factors.factor: No test or guard was seen on the spend summary path against a zero divisor. No gradual rollout or error-rate check was seen when the flag was switched on in production.

The change-event query read no production changes, although the flag provider showed a recent flag change. Flag toggles were not visible in the change feed the Investigator read, which weakened the link from onset to cause.

Argus checked the service right after reverting the flag, before the window it had said it would wait for. It judged the action withdrawn without a fair read of the effect. A person closed the incident in the same moment, so the record does not show whether the revert fixed the errors.

The paging rule needs the condition to hold for {rule_waits} before it fires. Shoppers therefore hit errors for {alert_raised - began} before anyone was paged, and no early signal tied to the flag was seen.

input.executive_summary: Shoppers on io-shop saw account pages fail. The error rate rose from {errors_before} to {errors_while_broken} on average and peaked at {errors_at_worst}, so {errors_rise} of traffic failed that otherwise would not have. The service was broken for at least {duration}, a lower bound, because it was not back to normal when the incident was closed. The cause was a feature flag, monthly-spend-feature, which turned on a code path that crashes with a division by zero. The alert fired at {alert_raised}, after the paging rule's wait of {rule_waits}. Argus reverted the flag to off. Its check ran straight away and still saw the incident's error level, so it judged the action withdrawn. A person then closed the incident from PagerDuty, kept the flag off and paged the checkout team. The record does not show the service recovering.

got_lucky: Only a share of account page requests failed, not all of them. The failing path was behind a flag that could be switched off at once.
went_well: Argus formed the leading candidate from the logs within seconds and tied it to the flag. The ZeroDivisionError log line and the flag-on evaluations pointed at the same cause.
The mitigation was quick and low-risk: reverting a flag, which touches no deploy.
A person kept the flag off and paged the checkout team, who own the follow-up.
went_wrong: The revert was judged withdrawn from a check taken before its wait window began, so the record shows no confirmed recovery.
The incident was closed from PagerDuty while the service still looked broken at the incident's level.
The change feed read no changes although a flag change existed.

input.root_cause: Switching on the monthly-spend-feature flag enabled a spend-summary code path that raises ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py, so a share of account page requests failed. The record does not show which input made the divisor zero, and no guard or test on that path was seen.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for a share of shoppers
